extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers and grant applicants (R01/K/F applicants, PIs, institutional research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing NIH grant applications (R01, K, F, supplements) that align with NIH leadership priorities such as rigor, data sharing, investigator status, budget productivity, and institute mission. Emphasizes what reviewers and NIH leaders (per Mike Lauer's Open Mike posts) value when funding decisions are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses an important biomedical problem within institute mission
rubrics_metrics.description: "Addresses an important biomedical problem within institute mission" (implicit rubric item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly state the biomedical problem and explicitly align aims with the funding institute's priorities; Lauer advises 'pay attention to institute priorities, not just CSR study section fit.' Emphasize significance and relevance to the institute's mission in Specific Aims and Impact/Significance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI not already saturated with funding / funding concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should "come from a PI not already saturated with funding" — a small fraction of PIs receive a large fraction of NIH funds; policy responses include the Grant Support Index (GSI) and similar caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH leadership views funding concentration negatively: the marginal R01 in a heavily funded lab is harder to defend. Demonstrate the need for additional support, distinct aims from existing awards, and cost-effectiveness. Be aware of policies (GSI/caps) and productivity-per-dollar findings (productivity declines after ~ $700K direct costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous, pre-specified methods
rubrics_metrics.description: "Has rigorous, pre-specified methods"; "Rigor is now scored explicitly in review"; "Statistical analysis plans must be pre-specified."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit rigor language: study design, blinding/randomization where appropriate, sample size justification, and a pre-specified statistical analysis plan or pre-registration where relevant. Reviewers will penalize failure to address rigor, so make methods and analysis plans clear and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological/chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how critical reagents, cell lines, antibodies, and other resources will be authenticated and validated. Provide authentication procedures, vendor/catalog numbers, and QC plans in approach or resource sections to avoid score penalties related to reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of sex as a biological variable (SABV)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sex as a biological variable must be addressed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether and how sex as a biological variable will be incorporated into study design, analysis, and interpretation, or provide strong justification for why it is not applicable. Address SABV in approach and analysis plans to satisfy review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan required and feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: "Data Management and Sharing Plan required"; "Reviewers consider feasibility and adequacy of plan; costs for data sharing are allowable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear, feasible Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan describing what will be shared, timelines, repositories, access controls, and estimated costs. Justify data-sharing feasibility and budget data deposition/sharing costs in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasible budget aligned with productivity expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Has a feasible budget aligned with productivity expectations"; "Productivity per dollar declines after ~ $700K direct costs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose a budget that is realistic and demonstrates value for taxpayer dollars. Avoid inflated budgets that are hard to justify relative to expected productivity; explain how funds will translate to measurable outputs and milestones. Consider NIH findings on diminishing returns when justifying large budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment supports reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Comes from a research environment that supports reproducibility."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional commitments, core facilities, oversight, data management infrastructure, mentoring, and quality-control processes that enable reproducible research. Reviewers look for an environment that materially supports the proposed work and reproducibility practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear training/mentorship plan for K and F awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Has a clear training/mentorship plan if it's a K or F award."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For career-development (K) and training (F) applications, provide specific mentorship plans, training objectives, timelines, mentor qualifications, and tracking of trainee progress. Make the pathway to independence and skill development explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrates value for taxpayer dollars
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame aims, methods, and expected outcomes in terms of public benefit and cost-effectiveness. Highlight potential translational impact, broad benefit, and stewardship of federal funds; reviewers and NIH leadership weigh value-for-money considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-Stage Investigator (ESI) / New Investigator considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: "ESI status (within 10 years of terminal degree, no prior R01); ESI applications get extra consideration at funding margins; Paylines for ESI are typically more generous."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eligible, claim ESI/new investigator status and emphasize independence and potential. Highlight institutional support and distinct contribution to strengthen funding margin consideration; be aware that paylines and policies may be more favorable for ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) and pipeline support
rubrics_metrics.description: "Persistent racial gap in R01 funding; NIH UNITE initiative addressing structural barriers; Diversity supplements, K awards, F awards as pipeline tools."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address DEI where appropriate (e.g., recruitment plans, outreach, workforce development, institutional initiatives). Use diversity supplements or K/F mechanisms to support pipeline development and describe institutional actions to mitigate structural barriers. Be mindful of UNITE and other NIH-DEI efforts when framing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate variability and limits in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Score-to-outcome correlations are weaker than people assume; Inter-reviewer reliability is moderate at best; NIH continues to study and refine review processes; Implicit bias training mandated for reviewers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that peer review has variability. Write for clarity and robustness: make significance, rigor, and feasibility obvious so that different reviewers reach similar positive judgments. Address potential bias explicitly in career/promotion and diversity-related plans where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage application volume and resubmission strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Themes: "Per-PI application rates rising; Resubmission churn is a known inefficiency; Resubmission scores often improve — don't give up after A0; Simplified review framework (2025) addresses some of this."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be strategic about submission volume: prioritize the strongest projects, expect resubmission (A1) can improve scores, and avoid excessive simultaneous submissions that may dilute focus. Use study section/institute priorities and summary statements to guide revisions under the expectation that resubmissions frequently improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align aims with institute priorities rather than only study section fit
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pay attention to institute priorities, not just CSR study section fit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly map the project to the receiving institute's mission and priorities in the application. While study section fit is important for review, funding decisions are made in the context of institute portfolios and priorities — state relevance in the research strategy and significance sections.
